plan: 2 Samuel 7:1-17; 1 Chronicles 17:1-15; 2 Samuel 7:18-29; 1 Chronicles 17:16-27; 2 Samuel 8:1-14; 1 Chronicles 18:1-13; Psalm 60:1-12

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.title: The Presumption of Cedar
readings.subtitle: A Misaligned Desire for the Uncontained Presence
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:1] And it came to be when the sovereign was dwelling in his house, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given him rest from all his enemies all around, [2] that the sovereign said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, but the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> dwells within curtains.” [3] And Nathan said to the sovereign, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you.”

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.title: The Divine Correction
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Mobile Dwelling Place
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:4] And it came to be that night that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Nathan, saying, [5] <dq>“Go and say to <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Would you build a house for <dn>Me</dn> to dwell in?</dq> [6] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have not dwelt in a house since the time that <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl up from Mitsrayim, even to this day, but have moved about in a Tent and in a Dwelling Place.</dq> [7] <dq>“Wherever <dn>I</dn> have walked with all the children of Yisra’ĕl, have <dn>I</dn> ever spoken a word to anyone from the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, whom <dn>I</dn> commanded to shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Why have you not built <dn>Me</dn> a house of cedar?’ ” ’</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.title: The Architect of Yisra’ĕl's Rest
readings.subtitle: From the Pasture to the Throne
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:8] <dq>“And now, say to <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, “<dn>I</dn> took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over <dn>My</dn> people, over Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off <dn>את</dn> all your enemies from before you, and have made you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.</dq> [10] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall appoint a place for <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and shall plant them, and they shall dwell in a place of their own and no longer be afraid, neither shall the children of wickedness oppress them again, as at the first,</dq> [11] <dq>even from the day <dn>I</dn> commanded rulers over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and have caused you to rest from all your enemies. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has declared to you that <dn>He</dn> would make you a house.</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.title: The Blueprint of the Eternal Seed
readings.subtitle: Establishing the Unbreakable Throne
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:12] <dq>“When your days are filled and you rest with <dn>את</dn> your fathers, <dn>I</dn> shall raise up <dn>את</dn> your seed after you, who comes from your inward parts, and shall establish <dn>את</dn> his reign.</dq> [13] <dq>“He does build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of his reign forever.</dq> [14] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am to be his Father, and he is <dn>My</dn> son. If he does perversely, <dn>I</dn> shall reprove him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.</dq> [15] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> loving-commitment does not turn aside from him, as <dn>I</dn> turned it aside from Sha’ul, whom <dn>I</dn> removed from before you.</dq> [16] <dq>“And your house and your reign are to be steadfast forever before you – your throne is established forever.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.title: The Execution of the Word
readings.subtitle: Nathan Delivers the Vision
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:17] According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Daviḏ.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.subsection: The Parallel Account of the Covenant
readings.title: The Contrast of Cedar and Curtains
readings.subtitle: A Sovereign's Misplaced Priority
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:1] And it came to be, when Daviḏ was dwelling in his house, that Daviḏ said to Nathan the prophet, “See, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is under curtains.” [2] And Nathan said to Daviḏ, “Do all that is in your heart, for <dn>Elohim</dn> is with you.”

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.subsection: The Parallel Account of the Covenant
readings.title: The Word of Correction to the Prophet
readings.subtitle: The Unconfined Presence of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:3] And it came to be that night that the word of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Nathan, saying, [4] <dq>“Go, and you shall say to <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “You do not build <dn>Me</dn> a house to dwell in.</dq> [5] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have not dwelt in a house since the time that <dn>I</dn> brought up <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, even to this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from one Dwelling Place to another.</dq> [6] <dq>“Wherever <dn>I</dn> have moved about with all Yisra’ĕl, have <dn>I</dn> ever spoken a word to any of the rulers of Yisra’ĕl, whom <dn>I</dn> commanded to shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, saying, ‘Why have you not built <dn>Me</dn> a house of cedar?’ ” ’</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.subsection: The Parallel Account of the Covenant
readings.title: The True Source of Terrestrial Authority
readings.subtitle: Subduing Enemies and Planting a Nation
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:7] <dq>“And now, say this to <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, “<dn>I</dn> took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [8] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off <dn>את</dn> all your enemies from before you, and have made you a name like the name of the great men who are on the earth.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall prepare a place for <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl and plant them, and they shall dwell in a place of their own and move no more, nor shall the sons of wickedness oppress them any more, as at the first,</dq> [10] <dq>since the time that <dn>I</dn> commanded rulers to be over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and <dn>I</dn> have humbled <dn>את</dn> all your enemies. And <dn>I</dn> declared to you that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does build you a house.</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of the Eternal House
readings.subsection: The Parallel Account of the Covenant
readings.title: The Promise of the Eternal Seed
readings.subtitle: The Unfailing Loving-Commitment
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:11] <dq>“And it shall be, when your days are filled to go to be with your fathers, that <dn>I</dn> shall raise up <dn>את</dn> your seed after you, who is of your sons. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> his reign.</dq> [12] <dq>“He does build <dn>Me</dn> a house, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> his throne forever.</dq> [13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am to be his Father, and he is to be <dn>My</dn> son. And <dn>My</dn> loving-commitment <dn>I</dn> do not turn away from him, as <dn>I</dn> took it from him who was before you.</dq> [14] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall establish him in <dn>My</dn> house and in <dn>My</dn> reign forever, and let his throne be established forever.” ’ ”</dq> [15] According to all these words and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to Daviḏ.

readings.section: The Posture of the Servant
readings.title: A Sovereign Stripped of Pride
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging the Unmerited Favour
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:18] And Sovereign Daviḏ went in and sat before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and he said, “Who am I, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? And what is my house, that <dn>You</dn> have brought me this far? [19] “And yet this was a small matter in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>You</dn> have also spoken of <dn>Your</dn> servant’s house for a great while to come. And is this the torah of man, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? [20] “And what more does Daviḏ say to <dn>You</dn>? For <dn>You</dn>, Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, know <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant. [21] “Because of <dn>Your</dn> word, and according to <dn>Your</dn> own heart, <dn>You</dn> have done <dn>את</dn> all this greatness, to make it known to <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant.

readings.section: The Posture of the Servant
readings.title: The Incomparable Elohim and His Exclusive People
readings.subtitle: The Ransom from Mitsrayim
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:22] “<dn>You</dn> are great indeed, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For there is none like <dn>You</dn>, and there is no <dn>Elohim</dn> but <dn>You</dn>, according to all that we have heard with our ears. [23] “And who is like <dn>Your</dn> people, like Yisra’ĕl, the one nation on the earth whom <dn>Elohim</dn> went to ransom for <dn>Himself</dn> as a people, to make for <dn>Himself</dn> a Name, and to do for <dn>You</dn> greatness, and awesome deeds for <dn>Your</dn> land before <dn>Your</dn> people, whom <dn>You</dn> ransomed for <dn>Yourself</dn> from Mitsrayim, from the nations and their mighty ones? [24] “And <dn>You</dn> have established for <dn>Yourself</dn> <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl as <dn>Your</dn> own people forever, and <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have become their <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.section: The Posture of the Servant
readings.title: Invoking the Strength of the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Pleading the Promised Blessing
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:25] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, the word which <dn>You</dn> have spoken concerning <dn>Your</dn> servant and concerning his house, establish it forever and do as <dn>You</dn> have said. [26] “And let <dn>Your</dn> Name be made great forever, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is the <dn>Elohim</dn> over Yisra’ĕl.’ And let the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant Daviḏ be established before <dn>You</dn>. [27] “For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, have revealed this to <dn>Your</dn> servant, saying, ‘<dq><dn>I</dn> build you a house.</dq>’ Therefore <dn>Your</dn> servant has taken heart to pray <dn>את</dn> this prayer to <dn>You</dn>. [28] “And now, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Your</dn> words are true, and <dn>You</dn> have spoken <dn>את</dn> this goodness to <dn>Your</dn> servant. [29] “And now, be pleased to bless <dn>את</dn> the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant, to be before <dn>You</dn>, forever. For <dn>You</dn>, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken it, and with <dn>Your</dn> blessing let the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant be blessed forever.”

readings.section: The Posture of the Servant
readings.title: The Posture of Absolute Surrender
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ Sits Before YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:16] And Sovereign Daviḏ came in and sat before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “Who am I, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>? And what is my house, that <dn>You</dn> have brought me this far? [17] “And this was a small matter in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, but <dn>You</dn> have spoken of <dn>Your</dn> servant’s house for a great while to come, and have looked upon me as though I were an exalted man , O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>. [18] “What more could Daviḏ add to <dn>You</dn> for the esteem of <dn>Your</dn> servant? For <dn>You</dn> know <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant. [19] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>Your</dn> servant’s sake, and according to <dn>Your</dn> own heart, <dn>You</dn> have done <dn>את</dn> all this greatness, in making known <dn>את</dn> all these great matters.

readings.section: The Posture of the Servant
readings.title: The Singular Name and the Redeemed Nation
readings.subtitle: Driving out the Adversaries
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:20] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, there is none like <dn>You</dn>, nor is there any <dn>Elohim</dn> besides <dn>You</dn>, according to all that we have heard with our ears. [21] “And who is like <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, the one nation on the earth whom <dn>Elohim</dn> went to redeem for <dn>Himself</dn> as a people; to make for <dn>Yourself</dn> a great and awesome Name, by driving out nations from before <dn>Your</dn> people whom <dn>You</dn> redeemed from Mitsrayim? [22] “For <dn>You</dn> appointed <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl to be <dn>Your</dn> own people forever. And <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have become their <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.section: The Posture of the Servant
readings.title: A Promise Foundational to Prayer
readings.subtitle: The Eternal Blessing on the House of Daviḏ
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:23] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the word which <dn>You</dn> have spoken concerning <dn>Your</dn> servant and concerning his house, let it stand fast forever, and do as <dn>You</dn> have said. [24] “So let it stand fast, and <dn>Your</dn> Name be great forever, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, is <dn>Elohim</dn> to Yisra’ĕl. And let the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant Daviḏ be established before <dn>You</dn>.’ [25] “For <dn>You</dn>, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, have revealed to <dn>Your</dn> servant to build a house for him. Therefore <dn>Your</dn> servant has found courage to pray before <dn>You</dn>. [26] “And now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, and have promised this goodness to <dn>Your</dn> servant. [27] “And now, <dn>You</dn> have been pleased to bless <dn>את</dn> the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant to be before <dn>You</dn> forever. For <dn>You</dn> have blessed it, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and it is blessed forever.”

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.title: Dismantling Hostile Infrastructures
readings.subtitle: The Subjugation of Philistia and Mo’aḇ
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:1] And after this it came to be that Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines and humbled them. And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines. [2] He also struck <dn>את</dn> Mo’aḇ, and measured them off with a line, causing them to lie down on the earth. With two lines he measured off those to be put to death, and with one complete line those to be kept alive. And the Mo’aḇites became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. [3] Daviḏ also struck <dn>את</dn> Haḏaḏezer son of Reḥoḇ, sovereign of Tsoḇah, as he went to restore his rule at the River Euphrates. [4] And Daviḏ captured from him one thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Daviḏ destroyed <dn>את</dn> all the chariots, but he left of them a hundred chariots.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.title: Expanding the Boundary of Peace
readings.subtitle: The Spoils of Aram Brought to Yerushalayim
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:5] And the Arameans of Dammeseq came to help Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, and Daviḏ struck twenty-two thousand of the Arameans. [6] Then Daviḏ put watch-posts in Aram of Dammeseq. And the Arameans became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went. [7] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold which were on the servants of Haḏaḏezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim. [8] And from Betaḥ and from Bĕrothai, cities of Haḏaḏezer, Sovereign Daviḏ took very much bronze.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.subsection: The Premial Wealth of the Kingdom
readings.title: The Consecration of the Plunder
readings.subtitle: Tributes Set Apart for YeHoVaH
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:9] And To‘i sovereign of Ḥamath heard that Daviḏ had stricken <dn>את</dn> all the army of Haḏaḏezer, [10] so To‘i sent <dn>את</dn> Yoram his son to Sovereign Daviḏ, to ask peace of him and bless him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏezer and struck him, for Haḏaḏezer had battles with To‘i. And Yoram brought with him objects of silver, and objects of gold, and objects of bronze. [11] Sovereign Daviḏ also set these apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, along with the silver and gold that he had set apart from all the nations which he had humbled: [12] from Aram, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalĕq, and from the spoil of Haḏaḏezer son of Reḥoḇ, sovereign of Tsoḇah.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.subsection: The Premial Wealth of the Kingdom
readings.title: The Dominion Maintained
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Secures the Victorious Path
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:13] And Daviḏ made a name for himself when he returned from striking <dn>את</dn> eighteen thousand Arameans in the Valley of Salt. [14] And he put watch-posts in Eḏom. Throughout all Eḏom he put watch-posts, and all the Eḏomites became Daviḏ’s servants. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.title: Striking the Adversary's Holdings
readings.subtitle: Reclaiming the Appointed Lands
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:1] And after this it came to be that Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines, and humbled them, and took <dn>את</dn> Gath and its towns from the hand of the Philistines. [2] And he struck <dn>את</dn> the Mo’aḇites, and the Mo’aḇites became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. [3] And Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah as far as Ḥamath, as he went to establish his power by the River Euphrates. [4] And Daviḏ took from him one thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Daviḏ also hamstrung <dn>את</dn> all the chariot horses, but left of them for one hundred chariots.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.title: Securing the Material for the Temple
readings.subtitle: The Bronze Harvested for the Future Sea
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:5] And when Aram of Darmeseq came to help Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, Daviḏ struck twenty-two thousand of Aram, [6] and Daviḏ stationed men in Aram of Darmeseq, and the Arameans became Daviḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went. [7] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold that were on the servants of Haḏaḏezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim. [8] And from Tiḇḥath and from Kun, cities of Haḏaḏezer, Daviḏ brought a large amount of bronze, with which Shelomoh made <dn>את</dn> the bronze Sea, and <dn>את</dn> the columns, and <dn>את</dn> the vessels of bronze.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.title: Economic Surrender of the Surrounding Kings
readings.subtitle: The Dedication of the Nations' Wealth
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:9] And when To‘u sovereign of Ḥamath heard that Daviḏ had stricken <dn>את</dn> all the army of Haḏaḏezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, [10] he sent <dn>את</dn> Haḏoram his son to Sovereign Daviḏ, to ask peace of him and bless him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏezer and struck him – because Haḏaḏezer had been fighting against To‘u – with all kinds of objects of gold, and silver, and bronze. [11] Sovereign Daviḏ also set these apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, along with the silver and gold that he had brought from all these nations, from Eḏom, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalĕq.

readings.section: The Expansion of the Righteous Dominion
readings.title: The Total Subjection of Eḏom
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Deliverance Manifested
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:12] And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah struck <dn>את</dn> eighteen thousand Eḏomites in the Valley of Salt, [13] and he put watch-posts in Eḏom, and all the Eḏomites became Daviḏ’s servants. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ wherever he went.

readings.section: The Standard of Truth
readings.title: The Refining Judgment of Elohim
readings.subtitle: Drinking the Wine of Trembling
readings.text: [Psalm 60:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have rejected us; <dn>You</dn> have broken us; <dn>You</dn> have been displeased; Turn back to us! [2] <dn>You</dn> have made the earth tremble; <dn>You</dn> have broken it; Heal its breaches, for it is shaken. [3] <dn>You</dn> have let <dn>Your</dn> people see hardship; <dn>You</dn> have made us drink the wine of trembling. [4] <dn>You</dn> have given a banner to those who fear <dn>You</dn>, That it might be lifted up Because of the truth. Selah. [5] That those <dn>You</dn> love might be rescued, Save with <dn>Your</dn> right hand and answer me.

readings.section: The Standard of Truth
readings.title: The Sovereign Allocation of the Earth
readings.subtitle: Treading Down the Adversaries in Elohim
readings.text: [Psalm 60:6] <dn>Elohim</dn> has spoken in <dn>His</dn> set-apartness, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> exult, <dn>I</dn> portion out Sheḵem And measure out the Valley of Sukkoth.</dq> [7] <dq>“Gil‘aḏ is <dn>Mine</dn> and Menashsheh is <dn>Mine</dn>, And Ephrayim is the defence of <dn>My</dn> head, Yehuḏah is <dn>My</dn> inscriber.</dq> [8] <dq>“Mo’aḇ is <dn>My</dn> wash-pot, Over Eḏom <dn>I</dn> cast <dn>My</dn> shoe, Shout loud, O Philistia, because of <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq> [9] Who would bring me to the strong city? Who shall lead me to Eḏom? [10] Have not <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, rejected us? And <dn>You</dn> do not go out, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, With our armies! [11] Give us help from distress, For the help of man is naught. [12] In <dn>Elohim</dn> we do mightily, And <dn>He</dn> treads down our adversaries!
